## Paper facts
Working title: "Free School Meals and Student Attendance: Evidence from
Zambia's District Rollout". Applied empirical; difference-in-differences
(two-period, district rollout — NOT randomized; poorer districts first).
Data: EMIS school-by-month panel, 1,840 schools, 2021–2023. Target: World
Bank Policy Research Working Paper. Stage: full draft, pre-submission.
Deadline: decision meeting with the Ministry in ~6 weeks. Sole-authored
(R. Demo, fictional). Formats: Quarto (paper), LaTeX tables.

## Grounding pointers
- Draft: `paper/draft.qmd`
- Outputs (tables/figures): `outputs/` (tab1_summary.tex, tab2_main.tex —
  col 2 preferred, tab3_het.tex)
- Bibliography: `paper/references.bib`
Rules for consumers: wb-paper-write takes numbers ONLY from these outputs and

## Positioning (human-authored)
- Main finding: "Free school meals raised attendance by about 4 percentage
  points, with the biggest gains for girls and rural schools." (human verbatim)
- Contribution: first at-scale evidence on school feeding from Zambia's
  national rollout · Type(s), ranked: evidence (1), policy (2)
- Relevance: "The Ministry of Education decides on national scale-up next
  year, and there is no Zambian evidence to base that decision on." (human
  verbatim)
- Claim sentence: "This paper is the best evidence to date on school feeding
  at scale in Southern Africa." (human seed + AI sharpening — chose variant A
  unedited)
Unsettled elements: none.

## Audience
Primary: Ministry of Education policy team + World Bank education GP
(decision-makers on scale-up). Secondary: PRWP technical reviewers; education
economists.

## Feedback priorities
- Wants: policy framing — "make the results usable for the scale-up decision
  without overselling them."
- Fears: "reviewers will say the parallel-trends assumption is untested and
  the rollout wasn't really quasi-random."
- From past reviews (see references/feedback/): (1) identification doubts on
  non-random rollout; (2) overclaiming beyond study population.

## Voice fingerprint
From the author's prior report (fictional): plain register; short declarative
sentences mixed with occasional long qualifying ones; "we" throughout;
states results flat, hedges mechanisms ("consistent with"); signature move:
opens results paragraphs with the number. British spelling.

## Conventions
- **results-by-para-3**: State the main finding, with magnitude, by paragraph
  3 of the introduction.
  - Check: magnitude appears in intro paragraphs 1–3.
  - Evidence: interview 2026-09-21, "I want the number on page one." (Part 2 Q3)
  - Applies to: introduction, abstract · Tag: structure
- **benchmark-every-magnitude**: Every headline effect is compared to a
  benchmark the Ministry uses (baseline mean, or a known intervention).
  - Check: each magnitude in abstract/intro/conclusion has a benchmark within
    two sentences.
  - Evidence: interview 2026-09-21, audience answer. · Tag: results
- **claims-stay-in-zambia**: No recommendation beyond the study population
  (Zambian primary schools) without an explicit external-validity caveat.
  `overrides baseline: none — tightens Conclusion › Implications`
  - Check: scan conclusion/abstract for geography of claims vs. evidence.
  - Evidence: references/feedback/referee-report-2024.md, "the manuscript
    generalises far beyond its setting" · Tag: policy

## Non-negotiables
- British spelling throughout.
- The acknowledgements text is not to be touched or flagged.

## Outlet constraints
- PRWP: abstract ≤ 150 words (guideline, binding). Provenance: PRWP author

- PRWP: disclaimer footnote required on title page (binding).
- AI-use disclosure: WB guidance (demo placeholder) — disclose AI drafting or
